title: An ideal multiple factors through a generic coherent inclusion
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $K,G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], let $a:K\to G$ be a monomorphism and let $\xi\in X$ be a point at which the induced module-stalk map is bijective [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There exist a quasi-coherent module $J$ and a monomorphism $\iota:J\to\mathcal O_X$, surjective on the $\xi$-stalk, and a morphism $\psi:JG\to K$ whose composite with $a$ equals the canonical inclusion $JG\to G$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. No integral closed subscheme or sum of ideals is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01YL, third proof paragraph: the annihilating ideal multiple lies in the ideal-sum submodule. Use the annihilator ideal of the coherent cokernel (Tags 05JU and 05JV). Source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YL.

proof.text: Form Q = coker(a). Coherent cokernel closure makes Q coherent. On the locally Noetherian scheme it is quasi-coherent and finite type.
The stalk of the cokernel is the cokernel of the stalk map. Since a is surjective at ξ, Q has zero ξ-stalk. In particular ξ does not belong to its nonzero-stalk locus.

Let H be the annihilator ideal of Q from scheme-theoretic support. It is quasi-coherent, its affine section ideals are the annihilators of the affine section modules of Q, and its closed support is precisely the nonzero-stalk locus of Q. The ideal zero-set stalk criterion therefore shows that H → O_X is surjective at ξ.

Put J = H.toModules and ι = H.toModulesι. The product inclusion JG → G followed by q : G → Q is zero: on every affine open its image consists of sums of jg with j in the annihilator ideal of Q, and q(jg)=j q(g)=0. Vanishing on the affine basis implies global vanishing by sheaf separatedness. Lift JG → G to ker(q) by the kernel universal property. Since a is mono, its image is canonically K and ker(q)=im(a); compose the lift with this canonical isomorphism to obtain ψ with ψ ≫ a = idealModuleProductι ι G. This argument includes zero cokernels and does not use compactness.

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_generic_mono_ideal_factor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {K G : X.Modules}
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace K)
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G)
    (a : K ⟶ G) [Mono a] (ξ : X)
    (ha : Function.Bijective
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).map a).hom) :
    ∃ (J : X.Modules) (ι : J ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf),
      Mono ι ∧ J.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      Function.Surjective
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).map ι).hom ∧
      ∃ (ψ : idealModuleProduct ι G ⟶ K), ψ ≫ a = idealModuleProductι ι G
